title: Mode flag: simulation and product read the sweep opposite ways
description: C3 is labelled a pathology simulation and its whole payload is watching personality distort group reasoning. Flooring agreeableness there deletes the phenomenon the harness exists to show. C5 has a human inside the system rather than observing it, where a bot that defers to a bad claim is a liability and the person harmed is the one least able to see it happening. Same machinery, opposite success criteria, so make the mode explicit rather than implied by which module imported it.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation mode lets the persona act on its weights unimpeded and records the damage. Product mode acts on the log and withholds. Constructing without a mode raises rather than defaulting.

title: Traits move evidence weights; log the counterfactual when it bites
description: Agreeable people genuinely weight testimony from people they like more heavily. That is an evidence effect, not a tone effect, and a ledger that scores all testimony identically has amputated something real. So traits reach the weights: openness sets how many hypotheses stay live, conscientiousness sets the evidence bar for reveal, agreeableness weights source credibility and governs concession. No clamping. Instead, when the persona would have taken a move that admissibility refuses, log both: what the trait wanted, what the ledger licensed, and the gap. The distinction being modelled is public compliance versus private acceptance. Agreeableness loads hard on the public side, so it fully governs the reply while the ledger records the private read that moved less.
acceptance_criteria: A withheld concession appears in the transcript with the trait value, the move the persona selected, and the missing evidence named. Nothing is suppressed without a corresponding log line.

title: Two-channel turn: persona-neutral reasoning, persona voice
description: Split each turn into two model calls. The reasoning pass updates the ledger and the board, runs the admissibility check and picks a move, at a low fixed temperature. The voice pass renders the chosen move in character using the compiled Ocean sampler. The failure this prevents is neuroticism widening temperature on the step that decides what is true. Note the scope limit: this separates sampler settings from reasoning, not traits from evidence. Trait effects on evidence weighting are P2's problem and are deliberately not solved here.
acceptance_criteria: Sampler settings from a profile reach the voice call only. A single-pass mode stays available so a learner can watch the difference.

title: Invert validate_solvability() into a runtime admissibility check
description: narrator-cby.7 built the epistemic clue graph and solvability check for generated mysteries: given the clues, does exactly one suspect survive. Turn it around. Given the ledger, is the conclusion the bot is about to state derivable from entries the user has seen. If not, the conclusion is inadmissible and the bot names the evidence it would need. Fair play as a runtime guard.
acceptance_criteria: A conclusion resting on an inferred-only chain is blocked and reported. The check runs on the ledger, with no access to the generator's ground truth.

title: Hypothesis board over live interpretations
description: Hold three to five readings of what the user wants, each with a weight, updated as evidence arrives. Premature collapse onto the first plausible reading is the single thing that makes a chatbot feel stupid, and the genre's engine is that the obvious suspect is wrong. Board is dumped on demand so a learner can watch weights move.
acceptance_criteria: A conversation that reverses direction shows the weight shift in the dump rather than a silent switch. Collapsing below two live hypotheses requires evidence that rules the others out.

title: Fair-play chat core: ledger, board, moves
description: The reasoning layer that makes the persona smarter rather than just better spoken. Four structures: an evidence ledger with provenance, a board of live interpretations, an admissibility check inverted from validate_solvability(), and an explicit move set. Same abstention spine as mathgraph and certabstain.
acceptance_criteria: Every conclusion the bot states cites ledger entries the user has seen; conclusions that cannot are withheld with the missing evidence named.

title: Evidence ledger with provenance tags
description: One append-only JSONL ledger per conversation. Each entry carries a claim, the turn it entered on, and a provenance tag: stated by the user, observed in an artifact, inferred by the model, or assumed. The distinction is the whole point, since testimony and deduction are not the same evidence and most chatbots blur them. Flush per line and reuse the file:line error context from load_transcript.
acceptance_criteria: A ledger survives a run killed mid-write and reads back with the offending line named. Every entry has a provenance tag; untagged entries are rejected at write time.

title: Anthropic backend: /v1/messages against claude-fable-5
description: Second backend hitting https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages with model claude-fable-5. Note the shape differences from Ollama: system is a top-level parameter and not a message role, max_tokens is required, and the response is a content block list rather than a single string. Key comes from the environment and never from source or a profile file.
acceptance_criteria: A conversation runs end to end against Fable; with no key set the failure names the missing variable instead of raising a connection error.

title: Model backend split: Ollama stays default, Fable opt-in
description: ocean.generate() POSTs to localhost:11434 directly, and agents.converse already takes an injectable generate_fn. That injection point is the seam. Formalise it so a second backend drops in without touching callers.
acceptance_criteria: Both backends satisfy one interface; every existing entry point runs unchanged against Ollama with no key set.

title: Extract a Backend interface behind ocean.generate()
description: Move the Ollama HTTP call into backends/ocean_ollama.py behind a small protocol: take a profile, a prompt and a model, return text. Keep Ollama the default so an offline learner sees no change. Stdlib only, per the PRD's legibility constraint.
acceptance_criteria: ocean.py no longer contains an HTTP call; existing self-checks pass untouched.

title: C5: Narrator as a fair-play chatbot
description: Turn the mystery engine around and point it at the conversation. mystery.py holds ground truth in WorldSimulation and checks with validate_solvability() that the clues reach the culprit. In chat the user holds ground truth and the bot deduces, so solvability becomes a runtime constraint on the bot: it may assert only what is derivable from evidence the user has actually seen. That is the Knox/Van Dine fair-play rule as a hallucination guard, and the same untrusted-producer/independent-checker split as certkit.
acceptance_criteria: A learner can hold a conversation, read the ledger and hypothesis board it produced, and point at the specific entry that licensed each conclusion. Every turn logs which move was chosen and why.

title: Reverse the 'local Ollama only' non-goal, on the record
description: prd.md lists 'No cloud model providers. Local Ollama only.' under Non-goals. Adding a Fable backend reverses that, for an audience of three teenagers. The change is real: API keys, per-token cost, network dependency, and their text leaving the machine. Record the decision and its scope before any backend code lands, and amend prd.md in the same change.
acceptance_criteria: prd.md no longer claims a non-goal the code contradicts. The decision states what stays local by default, what the cloud path is for, and who holds the key.

title: Discussion protocol and the unshared-clue measure
description: Run agents.converse over the partition and record, per clue, whether it was ever voiced, by whom, on which turn, and whether anyone built on it after. The classic finding is that shared information is mentioned earlier and repeated more while unique information stays unvoiced or gets dropped after one mention, so mention count alone is the wrong measure and uptake has to be tracked separately. Add the group's final answer and whether it matches the culprit.
acceptance_criteria: Per-clue voiced, uptake and turn-first-mentioned columns come out of a run. Group answer is scored against ground truth the agents never saw.

title: Clue partitioner with a solvability contract
description: Split the clue set across N agents such that the union satisfies validate_solvability() and every individual subset does not. Shared clues go to everyone, unique clues to exactly one agent. The partition is the experimental manipulation, so it needs to be seeded, recorded, and reproducible. Reject a partition that fails either half of the contract rather than running a degenerate condition and reporting it as a result.
acceptance_criteria: Union is solvable, every subset is not, both checked by the existing validator rather than by construction. Rejected partitions name which half failed. Same seed reproduces the same split.

title: Hidden-profile harness over the mystery generator
description: Stasser and Titus's paradigm: distribute information so no individual can reach the right answer alone but the pooled set can, then watch groups spend their discussion on what everyone already knew and miss the solution. The effect is robust in meta-analysis and it is isomorphic to what mystery.py already builds. The generator holds ground truth, the clue graph knows which clues are load-bearing, and validate_solvability() already answers whether a clue set narrows to one suspect. Partition that set across agents instead of handing it to one solver and C3 becomes an experiment with a correct answer rather than a transcript with vibes. The pathology it exposes is the one metrics.py already counts.
acceptance_criteria: A run reports whether the group reached the culprit, which clues were never voiced, and which agent held them. Ground truth stays out of every agent's context.

title: JSON schema + load/save for Ocean profiles
description: Profiles are currently literals in source. Define a JSON schema for the five traits and add load/save so profiles become shareable artifacts learners can pass around and diff.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip save/load preserves a profile; malformed and out-of-range files are rejected with a clear error.
close_reason: save/load with validation, round-trip and six rejection cases covered in self-check

title: C1: personality parameterization
description: OCEAN trait vector compiled into Ollama system prompts and sampling parameters. Core is built in ocean.py; remaining work is making profiles into shareable artifacts and handling the cultural transformation matrix responsibly.
acceptance_criteria: Profiles can be defined, saved, loaded, and demonstrably change model output.
close_reason: all child tasks complete

title: Narrator: codegen + psychology teaching project
description: Umbrella for the three components in prd.md: personality parameterization, graph-based motive generation, and multi-agent pathology simulation. Local Ollama only, stdlib-first, every component runnable standalone from the CLI.
close_reason: all four components built, self-checking, and pushed

title: Checker subagent carries no Ocean profile
description: Role-differentiated subagents rather than conversationalists: a high-openness proposer, a low-agreeableness critic, and a checker. Vale and Wren from C3 already cover the first two. The checker is the one agent constructed without a profile and without persona injection, because a checker whose judgment varies with its traits is not a checker. This survives the move away from floors: traits may weight evidence anywhere else, but the thing that audits the weighting cannot itself be weighted. Make it a construction-time error rather than a convention.
acceptance_criteria: Passing a profile to the checker raises rather than being ignored. Verdicts are reproducible across runs at fixed seed while proposer and critic vary.

title: Agreeableness sweep, scored in both directions
description: Sweep agreeableness from -1 to +1 through the C3 scarce-resource scenario and score the same run under both readings. In simulation mode, admissibility failures must track the trait: if they stay flat, the trait is not reaching anything that matters and the simulation is decorative. In product mode, concession rate must move while withheld conclusions stay clean: if a bad claim survives to the reply, the counterfactual log failed to catch it. One sweep, two assertions, opposite signs.
acceptance_criteria: Both assertions run from one sweep and fail loudly with the direction named. A flat curve in simulation mode fails as hard as a leaking curve in product mode.

title: Explicit move set: reveal, complicate, ask, abstain
description: Each turn picks a move before it picks words. Most chatbots only ever have reveal, and mystery structure is mostly about what you hold back. Log the chosen move and the reason next to the reply, which is the observable output the PRD requires of every component.
acceptance_criteria: Every logged turn carries a move and a reason. A turn whose conclusion fails admissibility cannot choose reveal.

title: Discriminating-question selector
description: Instead of a generic clarifying question, score candidates by how differently the live hypotheses predict the answer and ask the one with the widest spread. Columbo's one-more-thing: boring under every hypothesis except one. Cap at one question per turn. Anthropic's persona-vector work found that responses to underspecified queries push toward hallucination, so failing to ask is itself an error source rather than merely a missed opportunity.
acceptance_criteria: Given a board, the selector prefers the question that splits it and rejects questions every hypothesis answers the same way. Selection scores are logged.

title: Token budget and key policy for the teaching audience
description: agents.converse round-robins N agents over a growing shared transcript, so cost scales quadratically in turns. That is the loop that will surprise someone. Add a per-run ceiling that stops rather than silently spends, and document which components are cheap enough to run against Fable and which stay local by default.
acceptance_criteria: A run that would exceed the ceiling stops with the count and the limit named. prd.md says which components default to which backend.

title: Re-derive the trait-to-sampler mapping without repeat_penalty
description: C1 compiles conscientiousness into a tighter temperature and a raised repeat penalty. The Anthropic API exposes temperature and top_p but has no repeat_penalty, so that lever has no target. Either move it into the prompt injection or find a different knob, and write down which traits survive the port intact. Trait-to-sampler is sold as a teaching payload in the PRD, so a silently weaker mapping is a real loss.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the five traits has a documented compilation target per backend, and traits with no sampler target on a backend say so instead of pretending.

title: Do not let persona code assert a model identity
description: Fable ships with safeguards that answer some sessions from Opus 5 instead, so the model behind a turn is not fixed and sampling behaviour can shift mid-conversation. Persona construction must not name or assume a model, and the transcript should record which model actually answered when that is available.
acceptance_criteria: No prompt string names a model. Transcript records carry the responding model, or an explicit unknown.

title: Pooling metrics alongside the existing transcript measures
description: Extend metrics.py with the pooling measures: fraction of unique clues ever voiced, fraction that received uptake, and time-to-first-unique-mention. Report them next to turn share, agreement rate and concession so a learner can see the connection directly, since the agent who concedes most is often the one holding the clue nobody heard. Same command-line output style as the existing metrics.
acceptance_criteria: All three pooling measures print alongside the existing three from one saved transcript.

title: Trait and role conditions over the same partition
description: The manipulation the repo is uniquely placed to run: hold the partition fixed and vary the Ocean profiles. Predictions worth stating in advance rather than fitting afterwards. High agreeableness should suppress unique-clue voicing, since unshared information is socially costly to raise. High openness should raise it. A designated critic should raise pooling regardless of the rest, which is the argumentative-theory prediction. Record predictions before the first run so the harness can be wrong.
acceptance_criteria: Predictions are committed in the module docstring before results exist. A condition table reports pooling rate by profile with the partition held constant.

title: Clues do not actually narrow to one suspect
description: validate_solvability() only proves a path exists from Root to Deduction_Culprit, which is structural, not logical. In the seed-7 run the footprint is in the Library and Lady Margaret was also in the Library at t=2, so the clue set is consistent with more than one suspect. The deduction node currently asserts the culprit rather than deriving them. Clues must be checked to eliminate every innocent, or the mystery is unfair in exactly the way the PRD says it must not be.
acceptance_criteria: Solvability requires the clue set to be consistent with exactly one suspect; a seed whose clues underdetermine the culprit is rejected or regenerated.
close_reason: independent solver asserts exactly one consistent suspect across 20 seeds; under-clued mystery now fails validation

title: Epistemic clue graph and solvability check
description: Clues are nodes of believed fact, edges are inferences. Generated by traversing the causal layer under information asymmetry. The investigation must be a solvable DAG: an inference chain from available clues to the culprit must exist, or the mystery is unfair.
acceptance_criteria: Solvability is asserted programmatically; an unsolvable configuration is rejected rather than emitted.
close_reason: ported from source script, seeded, four bugs fixed; solvability asserted over 20 seeds

title: Causal reality graph as ground truth
description: Events as nodes, causal links as edges, over the simulated event log. This layer is what actually happened, held separate from what anyone believes happened.
acceptance_criteria: Causal graph is acyclic and every event traces back to the triggering act.
close_reason: metrics table over transcripts; causal layer asserted acyclic with causes preceding effects; alibis derived from shortest-path reachability rather than asserted

title: C4: three-layer mystery pipeline
description: From Mystery_Novel_Graph_Discussion.md. A generative mystery is three interconnected graph layers: spatial (rooms/doors), causal reality (ground-truth events and causal links), and epistemic knowledge (believed facts and inferences). Core principle: the deterministic logic engine is separate from the generative model, which receives node-scoped JSON payloads and never invents mystery logic itself. motive.py's psychological graph is the doc-1 instruction to psychologize this pipeline's nodes; this feature builds the pipeline it assumes.
acceptance_criteria: A seeded run produces a solvable mystery: ground truth, clues, and a chapter sequence consistent with it.
close_reason: all child tasks complete

title: Spatial graph and world simulation
description: Nodes are rooms, edges are doors. Simulate character movement over discrete time steps to produce a ground-truth event log. This is the substrate the alibi engine and clue generation both read.
acceptance_criteria: Seeded simulation emits a reproducible event log of who was where when.
close_reason: ported from source script, seeded, four bugs fixed; solvability asserted over 20 seeds

title: Agent turn loop with JSONL transcript
description: Spawn N agents from Ocean profiles, round-robin over a shared transcript with each agent seeing the conversation so far. Log who said what, under which profile, at which turn.
acceptance_criteria: A multi-agent run completes and writes a replayable JSONL transcript.
close_reason: round-robin turn loop, flushed JSONL transcript, injectable generate_fn so the loop tests without a model

title: Seeded traversal to deterioration path
description: Traverse baseline to crime, producing the murderer's psychological deterioration sequence. Must be seeded so the same seed yields the same mystery.
acceptance_criteria: Same seed reproduces an identical path; path is a connected walk through the graph.
close_reason: seeded weighted walk, reproducible, no revisits, verified over 40 seeds

title: Define bias/trigger node vocabulary
description: Enumerate the cognitive biases and psychological triggers that serve as graph nodes, with escalation weights on edges. This vocabulary is the substance of C2; everything downstream traverses it.
acceptance_criteria: A documented node set with weighted edges loads into NetworkX.
close_reason: 18-node vocabulary (5 triggers, 11 biases, 2 terminals), 31 weighted edges, validated loader

title: C3: multi-agent pathology simulation
description: Agents instantiated from C1 profiles converse over a shared transcript so learners can observe how trait configurations interact. Profiles are trait configurations, never diagnoses; agents carry descriptive names, not clinical labels.
acceptance_criteria: N profiled agents hold a multi-turn conversation, transcript logged to JSONL, basic interaction metrics reported.
close_reason: all child tasks complete

title: C2: graph-based motive generation
description: Procedural mystery generator where NetworkX nodes are cognitive biases and psychological triggers rather than locations. Traversal from baseline to crime yields the murderer's deterioration path, which doubles as the story outline.
acceptance_criteria: Given a seed, produces a reproducible motive path plus readable prose beats and a graph image.
close_reason: all child tasks complete

title: Chekhov ledger: unresolved threads with an age counter
description: Track threads that were introduced and never resolved, with the turn count since each appeared. Two uses: as a writing tool it flags guns on the wall that never fire, and as chat policy it drives pacing, since long conversations lose coherence from lack of pressure rather than lack of context. Threads are either paid off or explicitly retired.
acceptance_criteria: A thread introduced and dropped shows up with its age. Retirement is an explicit entry, not silence.

title: Extend metrics.py to score chat transcripts
description: metrics.py already computes turn share, agreement rate and who concedes over an agent transcript. Add the chat measures: abstention rate, how often the chosen question actually split the board, and the age distribution of unresolved threads. A learner should be able to argue with these numbers.
acceptance_criteria: Runs standalone from the command line over a saved chat log and prints all three, matching the existing metrics output style.

title: Chapters narrate out of chronological order
description: Root is the body at t=3 and alibi sightings are at t=2, so topological order narrates the discovery first and the earlier sightings after. Readable but not chronological. Fix means giving Root and Deduction_Culprit a t attribute and sorting the topological order by it. Found while building chapters.py.
acceptance_criteria: Chapters are emitted in an order consistent with both the DAG and event time.
close_reason: clue chapters now run oldest sighting first; Root stays chapter one since it is every clue's ancestor

title: load_transcript gives no context on a malformed line
description: converse() flushes one JSON object per line, so a run killed mid-write realistically leaves a truncated final line. load_transcript then raises a bare json.JSONDecodeError naming neither the file nor the line number. Found while building metrics.py.
acceptance_criteria: A malformed transcript line raises an error naming the file and the line number.
close_reason: load_transcript now enumerates lines and raises ValueError('{path}:{lineno}: {json error}') on a decode failure. ValueError is deliberate: json.JSONDecodeError already subclasses it, so nothing catching either type is affected, and metrics.py catches neither around parsing. _check_truncated_transcript covers the realistic case (a half-written object on the final line after a killed run) and asserts the reported line number is right even with a blank line earlier in the file, plus that a blank trailing line is still skipped rather than treated as corruption. agents.py, metrics.py and ocean.py self-checks all pass.

title: Alibi engine: spatiotemporal constraints
description: Rule suspects in or out by checking the event log against the spatial graph, so alibis are derived from the simulation rather than authored. Red herrings fall out of genuine ambiguity in the constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Given the event log, correctly partitions suspects into those with and without opportunity.
notes: Follow-on from 4.1: deduction is currently pure elimination — the footprint clue is corroborating decoration and does no work in the solver. A real alibi engine should derive opportunity from the spatial graph and event log (who could physically have reached the Study by t=2), so the trace clue narrows the field rather than just flavouring it.
close_reason: metrics table over transcripts; causal layer asserted acyclic with causes preceding effects; alibis derived from shortest-path reachability rather than asserted

title: Chapter generation by topological sort
description: Traverse the narrative DAG in topological order, calling the local model once per node with a node-scoped JSON payload. System prompt must enforce epistemic boundaries: a chapter may only reveal what is known at that node. Doc-2 used the OpenAI API; this project is local Ollama, so route through ocean.generate.
acceptance_criteria: Produces multi-chapter prose in topological order with no chapter revealing a fact not yet available at its node.
close_reason: topological chapter generation with graph-derived epistemic boundary; zero pre-deduction culprit leaks across 15 seeds

title: Transcript interaction metrics
description: Compute turn share, agreement rate, and who concedes over a transcript, so observations are measured rather than vibes.
acceptance_criteria: Metrics computed from a JSONL transcript and printed as a summary table.
close_reason: metrics table over transcripts; causal layer asserted acyclic with causes preceding effects; alibis derived from shortest-path reachability rather than asserted

title: Reference scenario: scarce resource split
description: The canonical demo from the PRD: a low-agreeableness/high-extraversion profile against a high-agreeableness one, tasked with splitting a scarce resource. Gives learners a concrete run to argue about.
acceptance_criteria: Scenario runs end to end from the CLI and produces visibly different behavior between the two profiles.
close_reason: scarce-resource scenario runs end to end; contrarian escalates 6-4 to 7-3 while accommodating holds 5-5

title: Render motive path as prose beats and graph image
description: Turn the traversal into readable story beats via Ollama, and render the graph visually so the structure is inspectable rather than abstract.
acceptance_criteria: Produces prose beats matching the path order plus a viewable graph image.
close_reason: mermaid render with path highlighting + ollama prose beats; example_motive.md renders on GitHub

title: Culture matrix: citation sidecar before any coefficients ship
description: transform() and load_matrix() exist; the default is identity and no population coefficients are bundled. Before any matrix ships, add a sidecar source field and require it, so every coefficient set carries its citation. Invented numbers keyed to an ethnicity are stereotypes dressed as psychometrics, so unsourced matrices must not load.
acceptance_criteria: A matrix file without a source field is rejected; a sourced one loads and its citation is printed on use.
close_reason: load_matrix now requires {matrix, source}; a bare 5x5 array (the old unsourced shape) is rejected. Eight rejection cases in _check_matrix_gate: bare array, missing source, missing matrix, empty/whitespace/non-string source, wrong dimensions, non-numeric entry. A sourced matrix returns a CultureMatrix whose citation is stripped, kept, and printed to stderr by transform() on every use. The identity path still accepts a bare list so tests make no claim about any population. Default remains identity; no coefficients shipped.
